name: GNG Electronics Ltd
title: GNG Electronics Ltd - 544455 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GNG Electronics Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% YoY to INR412.5 crore, with gross margin up 329 bps YoY to 24.65%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 32% YoY to INR412.5 crore, with volumes up about 18% and the rest from realisation gains. Gross profit was INR101.6 crore at a 24.65% margin, while EBITDA reached INR52.8 crore (12.8% margin) and PAT rose 56% YoY to INR28.9 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25-30% from 25% and PAT margin expansion guidance to 0.75-1% from 0.5%. Net debt rose by about INR100 crore QoQ to INR406 crore, while inventory fell to about INR700 crore from INR740 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR100 crore vs INR399 crore at end-Mar 2026
down from ~INR740 crore at FY26 end

segments.name: Geography: India
segments.commentary: Accounted for about 36% of Q1 revenue; standalone gross margin about 21%, below the group average.

segments.name: Geography: International
segments.commentary: About 64% of revenue; US 24%, Europe 23%, Middle East 12%, others about 5%. International gross margin was close to 30%, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 25-30% from earlier 25%.
FY27 PAT margin expansion guidance raised to 0.75-1% from 0.5%.
Management described guidance as conservative and said it aims to beat it.
Consol effective tax rate for FY27 to be assumed at 10-12%.
Management said it expects operating leverage to kick in soon, but employee and other costs will not rise in proportion to revenue.
capex_capacity: Business is asset-light with no material fixed capital; management described it as working-capital heavy.
Company holds 30-40 days of finished-goods inventory to support instant delivery to business and education customers.
Headcount rose to 2,420 as of June 2026 from 2,148, mainly in production, sales and customer support.
Supplies to 49 countries at end-Q1 FY27, up from 46 at end-FY26; customer touchpoints 5,130; supplier base 773.
Hiring and channel-marketing spend (dealer meets, EB Elite program, Chai Pe Charcha) was described as ahead of revenue.
demand_pricing: Memory prices rose a further 5-10% in the quarter; 8GB DDR5 at $126 and 16GB DDR5 at $231 as of June 30, 2026. Management said prices have risen about fivefold since October 2025 (corrected from 'doubled').
Entry-level 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD laptop price rose from INR40,000 to INR48,000.
IDC projects global PC shipments to fall 11.3% in CY2026, with a 20% YoY decline in 2H.
Management expects no meaningful memory relief before end-2027.

Sourcing: procurement prices have been largely matched to selling-price increases through buying ahead and contracts; disposition supply is expected to shrink as leases extend and purchases are deferred.

Management said it faces negligible competition in its served markets, which supports pricing. A US bank deal for about 60,000 desktops and a 3,000-unit laptop sale to an Australian customer were cited.

qa_highlights.question: Operating parameters: laptop and desktop unit split and geography mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Laptops 1,08,000 units and desktops/others 42,000; laptops 81% of revenue. Geography: India 36%, Middle East 12%, US 24%, Europe 23%, others 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and net debt trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital employed broadly flat; net debt up about INR100 crore to INR406 crore from INR399 crore at March 2026; capital employed marginally lower.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone vs overseas profitability gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisations are structurally better overseas and that deeper penetration is driving India improvement; no directional change expected.

qa_highlights.question: Split of gross margin lift between mix and like-for-like, and FY guidance for margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the directional split (India ~21%, international near 30%). It declined to give state-level or India-specific margin guidance, and instead revised the full-year guidance as above.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs realisation split of 32% growth; was there inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~18%, remainder from realisation. Management confirmed strategic inventory bought ahead of price increases helped gross margin and sales.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses up over 65% YoY; FY27 tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses up about 68%, attributed to channel incentives for better realisation and sales. Consol tax rate 10-12% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East disruption on UAE facility and freight?
qa_highlights.answer: No disruption; UAE facilities are operating and shipments continue by air. Management said the UAE government has managed the situation well.

qa_highlights.question: Procurement challenges and whether procurement prices are rising as fast as ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured material at near-old prices through contracts and services offered to vendors, and that it is building inventory and buying partners in advance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is opex growing ahead of revenue, and when will operating leverage appear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investment in people, marketing and channel meets is front-loaded. It expects operating leverage soon but said costs will not rise in proportion to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did growth slow to about 30% from 40% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Q1 a low-seasonality quarter and said growth will not slow down; it also reiterated its conservative guidance approach.

risks_watch: Net debt rose by about INR100 crore QoQ to INR406 crore in a working-capital-heavy model, with inventory of about INR700 crore.
Gross margin gains partly rest on inventory bought ahead of price increases; management said prices are still rising, but a price reversal would reverse the gain.
Revenue growth decelerated to 30% from about 40% in the prior two quarters.
Other expenses rose about 68% YoY and employee and marketing costs are growing ahead of revenue.
Lumpy procurement and dependence on large corporate and bank disposals; the disposition pool may shrink as leases are extended.
Middle East geopolitical risk, although management said UAE operations are unaffected.
Management gave a '30% to 50%' refurbished-to-new price ratio target in discussion, which it said was not guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, pricing power and margin levers. Cautious on hard numbers: it declined to give segment-level margin guidance, deferred on working-capital targets and corrected a memory-price figure during the call.
